description_full: Tecnoglass Holdings Inc. manufactures, supplies, and installs architectural glass, windows, and aluminum and vinyl products for commercial and residential construction markets in Colombia, the United States, Panama, and internationally. The company offers low emissivity, laminated/thermo-laminated, thermo-acoustic, tempered, silk-screened, curved, and digital print glass products. It also provides aluminum products, including bars, plates, profiles, rods, and tubes for use in the manufacturing of architectural glass settings, such as windows, doors, spatial separators, and related products under the Alutions brand name. In addition, the company offers curtain wall/floating facades, stick facade systems, windows and doors, interior dividers and commercial display windows, and hurricane-proof windows; StormArmour, that are attachment for sliding doors, and other products, such as awnings, structures, and automatic doors; and other components of architectural systems. It markets and sells its products primarily under the Tecnoglass, ESWindows, Alutions, Energia Solar S.A, ES, ES Imagine Extraordinary, Eswindows, Tecnobend, Tecnoair, Tecnosmart, ECOMAX by ESWINDOWS, ESWINDOWS Interiors, ESW Windows and Walls, Solartec by Tecnoglass, Solar Windows, Componenti, ES Metals, and E-skin, Prestige by ESWINDOWS, Eli by ESWINDOWS, Alessia by ESWINDOWS, Elite Line by ESWindows, ULTRAVIEW by Tecnoglass, and MULTIMAX by ESWIDOWS brand names through internal and independent sales representatives, as well as directly to distributors. It serves developers, general contractors or installers for hotels, office buildings, shopping centers, airports, universities, hospitals, and multifamily and residential buildings. The company was formerly known as Tecnoglass Inc. and changed its name to Tecnoglass Holdings Inc. in July 2026. Tecnoglass Holdings Inc. was founded in 1983 and is based in Miami, Florida.

financial_summary: Tecnoglass Holdings Inc. is a small-cap basic materials business with a $1.9B market cap on $984M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years and +15% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 27% against a 9% cost of capital — a 18-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 37%.

The business throws off $34M in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.85× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 39× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.4%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 45% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 23% operating margin runs 14pp above the Basic Materials median (10%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.79x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+16.6% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.04 across 219 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 29% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 20% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 42% and a beta of 1.02, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.01 vs 5y 1.03), so read it loosely.
About $10.2M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 72% in the 2020 crash and 41% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $37.60 (margin of safety -17%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 30%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $26.04 to $54.37 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Basic Materials peers: P/FCF 56.5 vs 22.8 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 12% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 1.8% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 11.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The 4 covering analysts target $55.75 on average, 27% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 27% clears the cost of capital of 9.3% by 18pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.57).
It runs a 37% gross margin and converts 4% of revenue into free cash flow.
ROE of 22% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.3x net debt to EBITDA ($104.1M of cash against $171.6M of debt), with interest covered 38.7x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.6, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 11.1% over 3 years, 21.3% over 5 years and 15.2% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 14%).
At current returns, reinvesting 46% of profits supports about 12.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -8.3% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.26 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 93% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 55%.
Capex runs 2.8x depreciation (10.3% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Its Rule of 40 score is 23, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 44.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 48%.
Insiders have only bought over the past year (8 purchases, net $27.0M bought).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.4% (1.4% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 1.0% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
Short interest is elevated at 13.1% of the float, 6.5 days to cover.
people: With about 9,601 employees, each generates about $102K of revenue, 0.2x the Basic Materials median, and productivity has risen 15.0% a year.
That works out to $4K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $5.1M (49x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (9/10, lower is better).
